newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Nov 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Nov 19.

text.p: The following is a summary of major South Korean political stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not gaurantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5650. Fax: (822) 727-5666.
- Urban home reconstruction in Seoul to be limited to 10,000 homes a year, or about 15 percent of 70,000 houses needing reconstruction.

- Obligatory hiring requirment imposed on corporations to be phased out, slashing about 200,000 people responsible for industrial health care, hazardous materials control, and other matters beginning next year.
- North Korea sends unoffical message to the United States indicating that it may express regret over the September submarine incursion incident.
- Government to allow corporations to obtain cash and commercial loans amounting to $3.5 billion next year as part of its compaign to bolster national competiveness.
- Firms allowed to get cheap foreign loans to help boost sagging economy.
- Limit on foreign loans eased: mandatory employment system to be phased out.
